posts.title: Bookmark - What is LinkedIn?
posts.description: A very well written essay (albeit much more positive and condoning than i’ll ever be about that site) on the mindless slop and cultural appeal that one can find in linkedin content. a succession of Pinterest slogans combined into verse, that seems so eager to express its depths of humanity that you instantly question whether it really has any. It’s a style of writing that reaches so hard for meaning, that it ends up as a set of free-floating signifiers, which refuse all interpretation. You can’t _mis_understand something that evades understanding altogether. The lack of conflict, the lack of humour, the lack of any tangible referents, creates the feel of a new kind of cyborg that seeks an eerie peace, honesty and consensus. If you asked the author (wherever they may sit on the human-LLM continuum) what they meant by any of it, they would be able to do little else than simply repeat themselves with even greater sincerity.

posts.title: Bookmark - After Twitter: Fragmentation, Platform Polities and Protective Sociality
posts.description: On the social media landscape following the ex-twitter crisis and transformation After Twitter registers the slow death of a set of ideals and related practices specific to platforms like Twitter, but also to the waning of ideals in relation to the communicative potentials of the open web more generally.
